confirmed.title: Trimmed end pieces turn the stream's own end into a raised, dry bank, which cuts the connection to the road crossing or other water
confirmed.scenario: An end piece is dropped at lines 197-200 because a platform vertex or other water lies within END_CLEAR. Everything after that is measured against the trimmed chain: q and yq (221-232), the outer raise (255-265) and the pond cut (240-247). The dropped stretch is still body (wet channel), so (a) its cover and envelope cells are removed anyway, because the bcell rule (body dilated by 2 rings) removes every cell touching the body; and (b) its vertices, now 3-14 m from the trimmed chain, fall in the outer zone and are raised as bank toward 'terrain behind'. The kit piece is gone, so nothing replaces the water. In EV108 kit-118 this happens at both ends: the upstream end at the road culvert is filled above the old water and the road, and the downstream end no longer reaches the other water it was trimmed for.
confirmed.verdict:
The defect holds, and it is in the EV108 output. In kit-118 the stream is cut off at the road and also short of the other water downstream.

How I checked: I read the code, then compared the real EV108 outputs with the EV107 inputs. I loaded terrain-ev107 against ev108-kit/terrain-kit.npz, cover-ev98 and envelope-ev107 against cover-ev108 and envelope-ev108, and rebuilt the kit-118 body the same way the script does. I did not rerun the script with END_CLEAR=-1, so the reviewer's no-trim values (6.43 / 6.67) are not confirmed by me.

Mechanism, read from the code:
- Lines 197-200 drop end pieces. Lines 221-232 then measure q and yq only from the trimmed chain.
- The dropped stretch is still body. Line 240-241 (bcell = body dilated by 2 rings) and line 245 remove every cover and envelope cell touching it, whether or not a kit piece replaces that water.
- Body vertices of the dropped stretch end up 3-14 m from the trimmed chain. They fall in the outer zone (line 255) and are raised by line 265 to min(seat(q), max(behind, need)). 'behind' (lines 257-262) is the highest original neighbour with a larger q in any direction. That includes high vertices beside the old channel, so the raise reaches the full seat height.

Upstream end, at the road (platform rows 559-561):
- The first kept piece (a short piece) has its upstream end at about (r 556.52, c 1377.81), y 6.67, from kit-records.json.
- Body end vertex (558,1377): H0 5.55, old plane 7.15, final 9.36. It is about 10.2 m from the chain start, so seat ≈ 6.67 + 2.74 ≈ 9.4. Its neighbour (557,1376) at H0 9.73 has a larger q, so 'behind' does not cap the raise.
- (558,1378) goes from 6.41 to 8.21, and (558,1379) from 8.21 to 9.64.
- The platform right next to them, (559,1377..1379), stands at 8.04 / 7.96 / 8.02. So a plug 1.3-1.6 m above the road and about 2.4 m above the kit water now sits between the road and the stream.
- Every cover/envelope cell in rows 553-558 around cols 1376-1380 is NaN in cover-ev108 and envelope-ev108. The water on the far side of the road (rows 561-563, planes 7.97-8.35) is kept, so the crossing through the road is blocked.

Downstream end:
- The last piece ends at about (r 512.94, c 1370.5), y 1.82.
- The cover/envelope cells between it and the remaining envelope cell (510,1370) were removed: cells (510,1369), (510,1371), (511,1369..1372) and (512,1369..1371). That leaves roughly 11 m with neither a kit sheet nor pond water.
- Vertex (512,1370) ends at 1.79, below the old plane 2.08: a dry hollow.

Docstring: the code follows its literal rules (drop end pieces; cut cells touching the body; raise the outer zone toward 'behind'). The docstring gives the reason for dropping as "a road over the stream is not cut". The result goes against that intent and against the connections requirement. Terrain is raised 3.8 m above its original height to above road level, and water is removed with nothing put in its place. Both are wrong geometry and lost water in the produced terrain-kit.npz, cover-ev108.npy and envelope-ev108.npy.

Lines: streambed_kit_v31.py:197-200 (drop), together with lines 240-247 (cut) and 255-265 (outer raise), which never account for the dropped stretch.

confirmed.title: The stones '~60 m' spacing uses straight-line distance from the chain start, not distance along the stream, leaving 166 m without stones
confirmed.scenario: sj is the Euclidean distance from A[0] to each joint, and line 296 places a straight-stretch stone when dist - last >= 60. On a meandering stream that distance stops growing or falls, so no stone is placed until the straight-line distance passes the previous value by 60 m. This breaks the docstring rule 'plus one every ~60 m otherwise'.
confirmed.verdict:
The claim holds, and it does change the EV108 output. The impact is low: it only changes where stones go and how many there are.

What the code does: tools/water/streambed_kit_v31.py:294 sets sj = ||joint.at - A[0]||. That is the straight-line distance from the first chord start, not the distance along the stream. Line 296 places a straight-stretch stone when dist - last >= 60, and line 299 then sets last = dist. On a meander the straight-line distance grows more slowly than the arc, and can even fall. The ~60 m spacing then stretches, and some sections get no stones until the straight-line distance passes the last value by 60 m.

This breaks the docstring rule at line 42 ("plus one every ~60 m otherwise"). It also misses the Chernarus density at line 11 (17 per km of streambed), which is a per-length measure.

How I reproduced it: I wrote a read-only script in a scratch directory and ran it with gis-env python -I against ev108-kit/kit-records.json. It rebuilds each chord start A from the piece matrices: centre M = T + R.(0, ROAD, 0), direction d = -Z in the horizontal plane, A = M - d.L/2. It also rebuilds each joint's turn angle as at line 219. The Euclidean rule gives exactly the published stone counts: kit-7 36 (36 in the output) and kit-118 4 (4 in the output). So I reconstructed the run faithfully.

- kit-7: axis about 1634 m of arc, but the largest straight-line distance is 1181 m. With the Euclidean rule, the largest gap between stones along the arc is 165.9 m. With arc length, the largest gap is 81.9 m and there are 39 stones. The reviewer got 40; my reconstruction of A is approximate.
- kit-118: 4 stones with the Euclidean rule versus 5 with arc length (largest gaps 86 m versus 64 m).

Fix: accumulate the chord lengths and use that as the joint distance (for example the arc s at each joint) instead of the straight-line distance from A[0]. That changes which stones are placed, so the EV108 stone records differ (count and positions). Terrain, pieces and pond cuts do not change, because the stones are placed after H is final.

confirmed.title: If every piece of a site is trimmed (or the axis is shorter than 6 m), the run crashes and writes no outputs for any site
confirmed.scenario: The front and back trimming loops (197-200) can empty the chain. Examples: a short stream lying entirely within 6 m of a road or other water, or a body whose axis is under 6 m, which builds no piece at all (162). Then line 221 builds A = np.array([]) with shape (0,), and A.min(0) at line 223 raises 'zero-size array to reduction operation minimum which has no identity'. max() over an empty generator at line 308 would also fail. The exception aborts main() before any savez or json.dump, so the outputs of all other sites are lost too.
confirmed.verdict:
I tried to refute this and could not, so the defect is real. The impact is a crash with no outputs. It does not corrupt geometry.

The claim holds by reading the code. Nothing checks that `chain` is non-empty between building the pieces and computing the bounding box:
- The piece loop at tools/water/streambed_kit_v31.py:160-163 breaks immediately when the axis is shorter than 6 m (`rem < 6.0` at i=0), which leaves the chain empty.
- The trimming loops at :197-200 (`while chain and piece_blocked(...)`) can also pop every piece.
- Line :221 then builds `A = np.array([])` with shape (0,), and :223 `A.min(0)` raises. I reproduced this with the gis-env python: `np.array([]).min(0)` raises "ValueError zero-size array to reduction operation minimum which has no identity".

The site loop (:131) has no try/except. All writes (np.savez/np.save :343, the json.dump calls :344-348) happen after the loop, so one empty site aborts main() and no outputs are written for any site. Line :308 (`max()` over an empty generator) would fail as well if execution got that far.

It does not affect the EV108 output. I read E:/DayZ-Baltic-Build/v31-pond-layer-20261013/ev108-kit/kit-report.json (schema streambed-kit-v31.v5):
- kit-118: 20 pieces, 2 end pieces dropped, axis 290.5 m.
- kit-7: 119 pieces, 0 dropped, axis 1649.5 m.

Both chains are non-empty, the run completed and the outputs exist. The failure needs a future site that is under 6 m long or entirely within END_CLEAR of blocked or other-water vertices.

confirmed.title: Slope guard can feed itself: it lowers the only movable vertex of a too-steep triangle even when that vertex is the triangle's lowest, then keeps sinking it until WALL_STEPS
confirmed.scenario: Valley wall at about 34 deg (or anything at 35 deg or more) inside OUTER of the axis. The trench or the axis fix deepens the floor, the guard lays back the first wall vertex, and the cascade climbs to the q<=OUTER boundary. There, a bad triangle has as its only movable vertex (line 320: touched & ~trench_all & ~frozen & ~protect_all) the lowest corner. Its other corners are untouched (q>14), trench/axis-moved, frozen or protected, and all higher. Lowering the lowest vertex of a triangle always steepens it, so the triangle stays above max(35, a0). Lines 330-332 pick that vertex again on every pass, and it drops 0.1 m per pass until WALL_STEPS=60 runs out. The result is a ditch about 6 m deep with a wall steeper than the one being fixed. The same happens next to a higher frozen platform or protected envelope vertex, and the ditch can sink an outer vertex below the 1.0 m engine-sea floor near the low end. Nothing checks that the move actually lowers the triangle's slope.
confirmed.verdict:
Confirmed by reading the code and running my own reproduction. In tools/water/streambed_kit_v31.py:330-332, `vs` holds only the movable corners of a bad triangle (movable = touched & ~trench_all & ~frozen & ~protect_all, line 320), and the code lowers max(vs) by height. Nothing compares that height with the triangle's non-movable corners, and nothing checks that the move reduces the slope. When the only movable corner is the triangle's lowest, lowering it makes the triangle steeper, so the triangle stays above max(35, a0). The vertex is then picked on every pass until WALL_STEPS=60 runs out (up to 6 m). The docstring says the guard lays the wall back; here it steepens it, which breaks that invariant.

Reproduction: I exec'd lines 316-335 unchanged on a synthetic 2048x2048 grid. The grid has a 34 deg wall rising east from column 100. Columns 98-102 are touched, 98-100 are trench, column 100 is lowered by 1 m, and column 103 is untouched. Result: wall_lowered=1417 (the loop never reached the break). Column 102 sank 5.8 m and column 101 sank 0.9 m. The slope from column 102 to 103 went from 34 deg to 58.6 deg. A higher frozen platform or protected envelope vertex next to the movable one triggers the same mechanism. This is a real defect for inputs with walls at about 34 deg or steeper within OUTER.

EV108: E:/DayZ-Baltic-Build/v31-pond-layer-20261013/ev108-kit/kit-report.json:117 records wall_lowering_steps=4. That is 4 single 0.1 m lowerings in total, and the guard reached its no-bad-triangle break, consistent with the reviewer's per-pass counts [2,1,1,0]. Its maximum lowering is 0.3 m, so the runaway did not happen there. I did not regenerate terrain-kit.npz myself; the reviewer says a rerun reproduced it bit for bit.

confirmed.title: Axis fix pushes every movable vertex with w>0.05 all the way down to roadway-0.03, whatever the size of the violation, and undoes need(q) and the sheet clipping on EV108
confirmed.scenario: A sample is crossed by a triangle whose interpolated height is a few cm to tens of cm above top. Lines 283-285 still set each movable vertex with w>0.05 to top, even bank vertices 3-7.5 m from the axis. Those vertices end below the visible sheet (roadway +0.25). The flat 14 m sheet then shows to about 5-7 m from the axis, which is the v3/v4 symptom the docstring says v5 removes ('se ven gaps'). It also breaks the docstring's need(q) rule ('keeping the sheet edge buried 2.75 m from the axis'). The code follows the documented rule; the problem is that the rule overshoots and the effect shows in the actual EV108 output.
confirmed.verdict:
The claim holds, and it affects the EV108 output. Lines 280-285 of tools/water/streambed_kit_v31.py lower a vertex whenever e > 1e-4, and every movable vertex with w > 0.05 and h > top is set to exactly top, whatever the size of e. No later step brings these vertices back up. axis_moved goes into trench_all (line 290), so the slope guard (movable = touched & ~trench_all ...) never touches them. The docstring does describe this step ('lowered to that target'). It still contradicts two other things the docstring says: need(q) for q <= 7 m, which keeps the sheet edge buried 2.75 m from the axis, and the v5 goal of clipping the 14 m sheet to 3-5 m.

How I reproduced it: I ran an instrumented copy of the file in my scratchpad. It saved h before and after the axis loop, plus q, yq and need. The inputs were the EV108 ones: terrain-ev107.npz, fp-ev107/footprint.npz, cover-level-ev98.npy, envelope-ev107.npy and ev108-kit/sites.json. The final heights match ev108-kit/terrain-kit.npz exactly (np.array_equal True).

Measurements, kit-118 / kit-7:
- Axis violations before lowering: p50 0.29 / 0.23 m, max 1.31 / 2.18 m.
- Lowering of the moved vertices: p50 0.97 / 0.98 m, max 2.17 / 4.37 m.
- Vertices moved: 56 / 334. Of those, 32 / 209 have q > 3, 10 / 45 have q > 5 and 2 / 19 have q > 6.
- Movable vertices with q in (3, 7] below need(q): 0 / 0 before the axis step, 32 / 204 after it, out of 61 / 371. The same vertices are also below the visible sheet (yq + 0.25).
- Example: vertex (155, 1489) at q = 7.47 goes from 5.94 to 1.57, with roadway yq = 1.60.

So bank vertices up to 7.5 m from the axis end up below the flat sheet, and the water shows well beyond 3-5 m. Scaling each vertex's drop to the size of the violation, and never going below top, would still meet the axis constraint. Setting vertices to exactly top is therefore an overshoot that changes the geometry, not something the constraint forces.

Not verified: the reviewer's visible half-width percentiles and the figures for the proportional alternative. I did not re-run those, and I did no in-game check. Severity: low.

confirmed.title: Site window is never clamped to the grid, so a chain within about 20 m of the map border crashes, and piece_blocked or tri_h silently read wrapped or empty slices
confirmed.scenario: Line 224: r0=int((ZTOP-hi[1])/6), r1=int((ZTOP-lo[1])/6)+1, c0, c1 with a margin of OUTER+6=20 m and no clamping. With r0==0 or c0==0, line 248 env[r0-1:r1+1, c0-1:c1+1] becomes env[-1:...], an empty slice. protect then has 0 rows and `frozen[sub] | protect` at line 250 raises a broadcast ValueError. With r0<0 or r1>=2048, H[sub], bd and cover[r0:r1] at lines 240-247 come out empty or truncated and no longer match the q/cq shapes, so the run crashes. In piece_blocked (lines 191-192), ra or ca <0 within END_CLEAR+6=12 m of the north or west edge makes blocked[ra:rb+1, ...] empty. The function returns False and a blocked end piece is kept silently. tri_h (line 106), used for the bank-land samples at line 153, wraps to the opposite edge (H[...,-1]) when a sample lies more than 6 m outside the grid.
confirmed.verdict:
The defect is real but latent, and it does not affect EV108.

Code reading of tools/water/streambed_kit_v31.py:
- Line 224 computes r0/r1/c0/c1 with a margin of OUTER+6 = 20 m and never clamps them.
- Line 191 does the same for ra/rb/ca/cb with a margin of END_CLEAR+6 = 12 m.
- tri_h (lines 104-106) indexes H[r0, c0], H[r0+1, c0+1] with no bounds check.

Slicing reproduction with numpy (gis-env python -I) on a 2048x2048 array: a[-1:31, 0:5].shape == (0, 5) and a[-2:5].shape == (0, 2048). That confirms the failure paths:
- With r0 == 0 or c0 == 0, line 248 env[r0-1:r1+1, c0-1:c1+1] is empty, so protect has 0 rows and `frozen[sub] | protect` at line 250 raises a broadcast ValueError. This is a loud crash, not corrupted output.
- With r0 < 0 or c0 < 0, sub at line 233 and the slices at lines 240/244 come out empty or wrapped, which also crashes on a shape mismatch.
- The silent cases are real too. In piece_blocked, ra < 0 or ca < 0 (a chord within about 12 m of the N/W edge) makes blocked[ra:rb+1, ...] empty, so it returns False and a blocked end piece is kept. tri_h on a bank sample past the N/W edge wraps to H[-1] and feeds a wrong `land` into Y.
- On the S/E edge, index 2048 raises IndexError in tri_h, and c1/r1 > 2047 truncate the slices, which crashes on a shape mismatch.

EV108 is not affected. I derived piece centres from the T column of every non-stone matrix in ev108-kit/kit-records.json:
- kit-118 spans x 8223-8273, z 8949-9199, about 3083 m from the nearest edge.
- kit-7 spans x 8319-9136, z 11147-12127, so the nearest is the north edge at 155 m.

With the ±12 m piece half-length and the 20 m margin, kit-7's r0 comes out around 20-21, consistent with the reviewer's (21, 1382). Every window, piece_blocked window and bank sample (≤ 10 m from the axis) therefore stays inside the grid. sites.json holds only these two sites.

I did not verify the reviewer's exact window corners, only these ranges. Severity is low: the defect is input-dependent and only triggers for a stream within about 20 m of the map border.

confirmed.title: End-trim 'other water' mask is built from every envelope cell, including dry ones, so the kit-118 outlet piece is dropped and the stream's last ~11 m end up dry
confirmed.scenario: kit-118: chain0 had 22 pieces. Piece 21 (short, A (8223.7, 9202.2) to B (8218.5, 9213.1)) was dropped because three envv vertices sit within END_CLEAR of it: (511,1370) at 3.27 m, (511,1369) at 5.40 m and (512,1369) at 5.42 m. Those vertices come from cells (510,1368) at 1.975 (envelope only), (510,1370) at 2.0 (cover) and (511,1368) at 1.975 (cover). None of these cells is in the fp-ev107 footprint, so none holds water: they are the stream's own dry cover/envelope continuation, with planes just below planes.min()-0.05 = 2.025. The pond cut (bcell, line 245) still removes the stream's own visible cells beyond the new chain end: (511,1369..1371) and (512,1369..1372), fp-ev107 planes 2.03-2.17, all visible. From z 9204.6 (last B) to z 9216, about 11 m, there is now neither pond nor kit water. On the axis at (8220.5, 9209): H0 1.53, kit terrain 1.79, old water 2.075. That point had 0.55 m of water and is now a dry dip 0.28 m below the old level.
confirmed.verdict:
The defect is real and it affects the EV108 output. I reproduced it with a scratch copy of the script that only adds logging, run on the EV108 inputs. The copy's outputs are identical to the published ones: envelope-ev108 and cover-ev108 have the same NaN masks with a max diff of 0, terrain-kit heights have a max diff of 0, and kit-records.json is equal.

What happens at tools/water/streambed_kit_v31.py:184: `fin` marks every envelope-ev107 cell whose plane falls outside [planes.min()-0.05, planes.max()+0.05]. For kit-118, planes.min() is 2.075, so the window starts at 2.025. Lines 185-188 turn those cells into the `envv` vertex mask, and lines 199-200 use it to drop end pieces.

For kit-118, chain0 has 22 pieces. Piece 21 (short, A (8223.7, 9202.2) to B (8218.5, 9213.1)) is blocked only by envv vertices: (511,1370) at 3.27 m, (511,1369) at 5.40 m and (512,1369) at 5.42 m. None of them is frozen. Piece 0 is dropped separately, by frozen vertices (558,1376) and (559,1377) at exactly 6.0 m.

The cells behind those three vertices are dry:
- (510,1368) is envelope only, plane 1.975.
- (510,1370) is cover, plane 2.0. Its corners are 2.79, 3.09, 2.89 and 3.03.
- (511,1368) is cover, plane 1.975. Its corners are 3.14, 2.92, 3.13 and 3.13.

Every corner of the two cover cells stands above its plane. None of the three cells has a plane in fp-ev107/footprint.npz, which is the only source of pond pieces (pond_author_v31.py:84 reads cells = isfinite(plane)). The EV108 footprint (ev108-kit/bury-work/fp0/footprint.npz) has no plane cells anywhere in rows 504-519, cols 1364-1375. Within 60 m of the chain end there is no footprint cell with a plane outside the body's range.

The nearest real water is the ev96_converted_to_sea channel at rows 503-506, col 1369, with terrain at 0.32-0.63 m. It is roughly 30-50 m away, well outside END_CLEAR (6 m). So the cells the code treats as other water are the stream's own dry cover/envelope continuation, not water. The docstring calls envelope cells "other water", but the data shows they are dry.

The consequence: the pond cut at line 245 still removes the stream's own visible cells beyond the new chain end, (511,1369..1371) and (512,1369..1372), with EV107 planes 2.03-2.17. The last remaining kit piece has its centre at z 9198.5 and ends near z 9204.6. The old water reached about z 9216, so roughly 11 m now has neither pond water nor kit water.

At (8220.5, 9209) the interpolated terrain is 1.547 in EV107, 1.794 in terrain-kit and 1.794 in terrain-ev108. The old water level there was 2.075, so the point used to be under water and is now a dry dip. kit-report.json is consistent with this: kit-118 has pieces = 20 and end_pieces_dropped = 2.

A mask built from the footprint planes (the water that is actually emitted) instead of the envelope would not block piece 21.

Not verified: how it looks in the client.

confirmed.title: Pond cut removes water from body parts the kit never reaches; old meander and side-arm beds beyond OUTER are left as closed dry pits up to 2 m deep
confirmed.scenario: kit-7, first pit: vertex (31,1387) at (8322, 12096). Old pond plane 5.025 over terrain 4.09 (0.94 m of water). It is at q = 15.8 m, beyond OUTER, so the terrain pass leaves it unchanged. The cut removes cells (30..32, 1386..1388) through bcell. The outer pass raises neighbours (31,1388) from 3.03 to 6.15 and (30,1387) from 3.83 to 6.48 (raise_to = min(seat, max(behind, need)), and 'behind' takes the highest farther neighbour). A priority flood on the native-triangulation vertex graph gives closed-depression depth 0.99 m before and 2.06 m after (spill 6.15). After the run no fp-ev108 pond cell touches the pit, and at q > 7 no kit sheet covers it. Second pit: vertex (99,1429) at (8574, 11688), an old meander that the smoothed chain cuts across. Old water 4.47-4.50 over 4.04. Before the run it drained into the stream (depth 0). The meander cells (97..101, 1426..1429) are cut, and (99,1428) is raised from 2.63 to 5.76 and (100,1429) from 3.22 to 6.69. The result is a closed dry pit 1.72 m deep.
confirmed.verdict:
Confirmed on the EV108 files. I reproduced it with read-only numpy in my scratchpad, using terrain-ev107 against terrain-kit (terrain-kit is byte-equal to terrain-ev108), fp-ev107 against v5a-run/fp-ev108, cover-level-ev98 against cover-ev108, and envelope-ev107 against envelope-ev108.

How the code causes it: at tools/water/streambed_kit_v31.py:240-245, bcell is the 2-ring dilation of the whole wet body. Every body cover or envelope cell whose plane falls in the body's range is cut, however far it lies from the chord chain. Lines 255 and 263-265 then reshape only q <= OUTER (14 m). There, raise_to = min(seat, max(behind, need)) raises the vertices between an old side pool and the trench. Nothing re-fills or re-checks drainage beyond OUTER. The docstring's ponds rule ("within CUT_Q of the chain or touch the body (2 rings)") describes exactly this cut, so the code is not drifting from its spec. The rule itself produces wrong geometry in the output.

kit-7, first pit, vertex (31,1387) at (8322, 12096):
- q to the nearest placed piece chord is 15.79 m, so the vertex is outside OUTER and outside every 7 m half-sheet.
- Its height stays 4.09 before and after.
- The old plane over cells (29..32, 1385..1388) was 5.025-5.05 in fp-ev107, cover and envelope. All of those cells are NaN after the run.
- Neighbours were raised: (31,1388) from 3.03 to 6.15 and (30,1387) from 3.83 to 6.48.
- A priority flood on the native 6-neighbour vertex graph (120x120 window clipped at row 0) gives a closed-depression depth of 0.99 m before (spill 5.08) and 2.06 m after (spill 6.15).

kit-7, second pit, vertex (99,1429) at (8574, 11688):
- q is 15.29 m and its height stays 4.04.
- The old planes 4.425-4.55 are all removed.
- (99,1428) went from 2.63 to 5.76 and (100,1429) from 3.22 to 6.69.
- Depth is 0.00 before (it drained) and 1.72 m after (spill 5.76).

Scale, from my own count (placed chords taken from kit-records): footprint cells cut with centre more than 7 m from every placed chord are 290 in kit-7 and 48 in kit-118. Of these, 121 and 16 still have a corner below the old plane, with max 0.96 m and 0.51 m. The reviewer reported 205/103 for kit-7 and 48/16 for kit-118. The kit-7 count differs, probably because of how the chord chain is taken, but the order of magnitude matches.

Refutation attempts that failed:
- No water is left over these pits: fp-ev108, cover and envelope are all NaN there.
- No kit sheet reaches them: q is over 15 m, against the 7 m sheet half-width.
- The pits are not a pre-existing shape: one was 0.99 m deep and full of water, the other drained, and both are now dry closed holes of 1.7-2.1 m, deepened by the outer raise.

The output change is degradation: dry closed pits where pond water used to be. It is not a crash or data loss. The defect is in the cut rule at lines 240-245 together with the outer raise at lines 263-265.

confirmed.title: Body-touch cut is clipped to the chain bbox window, so 9 kit-118 envelope cells that the docstring rule says to remove survive
confirmed.scenario: kit-118: window c0 = 1367 (chain bbox minus 20 m). The 2-ring body dilation reaches vertex column 1367, so bcell would include cells in column 1366. Cells (521..529, 1366) have envelope planes 3.275-3.575, inside the body range [2.025, 7.2], and bcell is True for all of them. They fall outside arr[r0:r1, c0:c1], so they stay in envelope-ev108.npy. Today they are dry: corners 4.6-5.2 against planes 3.3-3.6, and they are not in the footprint. A later shoreline pass could still revive them as orphan cells of a pond that has been removed. In general, body vertices reach up to 15.8 m from the chain and bcell extends 2 rings plus one cell beyond them, while the window margin is only about 20 m from the bbox of the chord endpoints. A body tail past dropped end pieces, or a side arm, would therefore keep visible cover cells as an isolated fragment next to the cut ones.
confirmed.verdict:
The claim holds. I reproduced it exactly, and the impact is low.

Code: lines 235-247 compute cq, bcell and blk only over the window arr[r0:r1, c0:c1]. The window comes from line 224, which takes the chord bbox plus OUTER + 6, about 20 m. Line 240 dilates the full-grid body but then slices it to [r0:r1+1, c0:c1+1], so any body-touch cell outside the window is never tested. The docstring's ponds rule (cells within CUT_Q of the chain or touching the body by 2 rings, with a plane in the body's range) has no window limit, so the code breaks a stated invariant.
